title: Floot vs Lovable: Which AI App Builder Is Better in 2025?
summary: Floot and Lovable can both be driven from Claude or ChatGPT — the real difference in 2026 is whether that build spends a second AI bill.
body_markdown:
Floot and Lovable both build web apps from a description, and both can be driven from Claude or ChatGPT. The difference that matters is who does the building — and who bills you for it.


## What Is Floot?


Floot is primarily a **connector you add to ChatGPT or Claude** , so you build your app by talking to the AI assistant you already use, in the app you already use. Floot also has its own in-app editor and AI agent, a fine way to work too.


Either way you build, Floot hosts the app, runs a real Postgres database, and handles auth, serverless endpoints, custom domains, and publishing — including converting your app into a mobile app on the Power plan.


### Core Floot Features


- **Connector-first building:** Add Floot to Claude or ChatGPT and build by chatting with the assistant you already use.
- **Own editor:** Floot's in-app editor and AI agent are a full alternative path.
- **Built-in infrastructure:** Real Postgres database, authentication, and serverless endpoints out of the box.
- **Publishing:** Web publishing plus custom domains, and mobile app conversion on the Power plan.


## What Is Lovable?


Lovable is an AI development platform for creating and iterating on web apps through natural language. It's grown well past the quick-prototyping tool it started as — it handles fuller applications now, and it's one of the most recognisable names in the category.


Lovable has also shipped its own official MCP server, so a Lovable project can be started or driven from a message inside ChatGPT or Claude. That's real and worth crediting — what it actually does is the next section.


### Core Lovable Features


- **Natural language interaction:** Iterate on your app by chatting with Lovable's AI.
- **Real code generation:** Access to the underlying code if you want to work in it directly.
- **MCP server:** An official MCP server exposes projects, chat, files, and deploys from ChatGPT and Claude — building through it still spends Lovable's own credits.
- **Fast prototyping:** Strong at quickly visualizing and iterating on web app concepts.


## The Real Difference: One AI Bill, or Two


This is the part that actually matters, and it's easy to get backwards if you only look at whether a tool is "reachable from Claude or ChatGPT" — both of these are now.


**Lovable's connector is a remote control for Lovable's own agent.** Ask Claude to build something through Lovable's MCP server, and your prompt gets forwarded to Lovable's agent, which builds on Lovable's infrastructure and spends Lovable credits to do it. That means you're carrying two bills for one build: the Claude or ChatGPT subscription you already pay for, and Lovable's credits on top of it.


**Floot's connector is a different shape.** It hands your assistant the primitives — read and write files, run SQL, typecheck, deploy — and your assistant does the thinking and writes the code itself.


Nothing else is running. No second agent means no second AI bill: building on Floot costs the Claude or ChatGPT subscription you already pay for.


Buying AI through a builder also costs more. A month of credits doesn't buy much building, which is why reviewers routinely report real Lovable spend landing at several times the advertised plan price: the allowance runs out, and you top up to keep going. The same money spent directly on a Claude or ChatGPT subscription goes a great deal further, because none of it is paying a middleman for tokens.


And there's the part that stings most in practice: a credit is spent when you send the message, not when you like the answer. Ask for something, dislike the result, ask again — that's two credits gone. Building through your own assistant, that retry is just more of the subscription you already pay for.


There's a second, quieter consequence of Floot's shape: because your own assistant is doing the building, whatever else is in that session comes with it — a Figma connector, other MCP tools, files you've uploaded, instructions you've already given it. Lovable's agent never sees any of that; it only receives the prompt string that gets forwarded to it.

## How Each Platform Bills You


**Floot** charges for the platform rather than the AI: **actions** — the edits, reads, and tests your assistant runs against your project — and hosting. Not tokens. There's a free tier and paid plans above it, with higher tiers adding custom domains, badge removal, priority support, and mobile app conversion. Building through your own Claude or ChatGPT account runs on the subscription you already have, billed by Anthropic or OpenAI directly. (Mobile publishing still requires your own Apple/Google developer accounts, and iOS builds need Xcode, which needs a Mac.)


**Lovable** bundles the platform and the AI into a single vendor-billed subscription: a free tier with a limited credit pool, and paid tiers above it that scale up the monthly credit allowance, with a higher tier adding SSO and a security center for larger teams.


Floot's actions reset daily, so worst case you hit the ceiling and you're back to building tomorrow. A Lovable credit pool is monthly — spend it early and you're either buying more or waiting for the next billing cycle.


## Best Use Cases for Each Platform


**Choose Floot if you want to:**


- Build by talking to Claude or ChatGPT, the assistant you already use daily, without adding a second AI bill on top of that subscription
- Have your assistant's other context — a Figma connector, other tools, files you've uploaded — available while it builds
- Have a full in-app editor and agent available as an alternative path (which does use Floot credits)
- Convert your app into a mobile app (Power plan)


**Choose Lovable if you want to:**


- Iterate quickly inside Lovable's own chat-based interface
- Work with a platform that has scaled significantly, and optionally trigger its agent from Claude or ChatGPT via its official MCP server — knowing that still spends Lovable credits on top of your Claude/ChatGPT subscription
- Prefer a single vendor-billed subscription over managing a separate AI account


## Which Should You Pick in 2026?


Lovable is a capable product and a fast way to get from an idea to something working. If you want to stay inside its own interface, or you're fine paying Lovable's credits on top of your AI subscription in exchange for that convenience, it remains a strong option.


Floot's bet is different: your own assistant does the actual building, using primitives Floot exposes to it, so there's no second agent and no second AI bill — the AI cost is the Claude or ChatGPT subscription you're already paying, plus Floot's actions and hosting meters. If you'd rather build inside the assistant you already pay for, with everything else in that session along for the ride, that's the more direct fit.
